No, I can't say that I have. I don't really do things automatically or get into trances. I'm usually pretty hyper-focused on what I'm doing, especially when I'm working.

Kevin is great, but he types so loudly. He has one of those mechanical keyboards with the cherry blue switches, and it sounds like a machine gun going off in the cubicle next to me. I've asked him to put O-rings on the keys to dampen the sound, but he says it ruins the \"tactile feedback.\" \n\nBut yeah, to answer your question, no. Just me.\n\nDoctor: Since that night during the cutover, have you ever experienced any other episodes where you couldn't remember important personal information or felt detached from yourself or your surroundings?\n\nPatient: No, I really haven't. We had this contractor come in last year—guy named Todd, always wore these cargo shorts with way too many pockets, even though it's freezing in the server room—and he was supposed to organize the network switches. But he ended up just zip-tying everything into these massive, tangled bundles. We call it the \"spaghetti monster\" now. If you need to trace a single ethernet cable, you basically have to detach the entire bundle and start from scratch. It takes hours. I keep meaning to go in there on a weekend and redo it all with proper color-coded Velcro straps. I found this great bulk pack of them online, they come in neon green, blue, red, and yellow. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
No, I haven't. I've always just felt like myself. I mean, my preferences haven't changed or anything. I still like the same things, act the same way. 

Though, you know, speaking of preferences, the new cafeteria vendor they brought in last month completely changed the coffee they serve. It used to be this really robust dark roast, but now it's this weak, acidic blonde roast that just tastes like hot water with a hint of dirt. Everyone is complaining about it. My manager, Susan—she's the one who always wears those really loud, chunky statement necklaces that clack against her desk when she types—she actually started a petition to bring the old coffee back. She got like fifty signatures in one afternoon. 

I don't even drink coffee that much anymore, to be honest. I switched to green tea a few years ago because I read it was better for your metabolism. I buy these loose-leaf teas from this little shop downtown. The owner is this older guy, Henry, who always tells these incredibly long stories about his travels in Japan. Last time I was there, he spent twenty minutes explaining the exact temperature the water needs to be for different types of sencha. It was fascinating, but I ended up being late for a meeting with the network security team. 

They were implementing this new two-factor authentication protocol, and let me tell you, the pushback from the sales team was unbelievable. They acted like typing in a six-digit code was the hardest thing in the world... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. What was the question? Oh, feeling confused about who I am? No, no, nothing like that. I'm just me.

No, I haven't. I mean, stress is stress, but I don't turn into a different person or take on some weird role when things get intense. I handle it the same way I always do. 

Although, speaking of extreme stress, you should have seen the panic when the air conditioning went out in the server room last Tuesday. It was like a disaster movie. The facilities manager, Dave—he's this guy who always wears those cargo shorts with about a million pockets, even in the dead of winter, and he's completely obsessed with his fantasy football league—he couldn't figure out how to override the system to get the backup chillers online.

I actually had a headache for two days straight after that. I tried taking ibuprofen, but it didn't really touch it. I usually prefer to use this peppermint essential oil roller on my temples when I get a headache, it creates this nice cooling sensation. My niece got it for me when she went to this holistic wellness retreat in Sedona. She came back talking all about energy vortexes and aura cleansing, which, honestly, sounded a bit out there to me, but she seemed to really enjoy it... 

Wait, what was the question? Acting differently under stress? Oh, yeah, no. I'm just me, even when the servers are practically on fire.
